source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Spark serialization, compression, configuration, and SQL tuning documentation; current Apache Parquet encoding, compression, and configuration specifications; Apache Avro 1.12.0; current Protocol Buffers wire/evolution documentation; current Apache Arrow columnar/IPC specification; current Apache Flink serialization/evolution documentation; and RFC 8878. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Format-, encoding-, codec-, and runtime-specific behavior is attributed.

evidence: Reviewed encoded bytes U, compressed bytes V, ratio r=U/V, bottleneck bandwidth, serialization/compression/transfer/decompression/reconstruction times, and encode/decode memory notation.
Reviewed lifetime read count, frame/block size and nominal count, physical write/read amplification, and per-frame failure notation.
Checked that logical values, in-memory representation, encoded bytes, compressed bytes, framed payload, and physical transferred/stored bytes remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Compression ratio explicitly names its denominator convention, and the timing equation is labeled as a non-overlapped approximation rather than a universal pipeline theorem.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced 24.0 seconds uncompressed at ratio 1.00, 21.0 seconds for the fast codec at ratio 2.00, and 30.0 seconds for the dense codec at ratio 3.33.
Recomputed the compact example from two seconds each serialization/deserialization, payloads of 1000/500/300 MiB at 50 MiB/s, and codec costs of 0/7/20 seconds.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 24 seconds uncompressed versus 20 seconds compressed: 8 seconds transfer plus 8 codec plus 4 shared seconds.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable fixture exposed and corrected an initial dense-codec arithmetic typo before completion; the reviewed value is 30.0 seconds.

evidence: Verified that the simple sequential transfer-time saving is (U-V)/B and that compression wins only when total avoided work exceeds codec/buffering costs.
Verified that larger blocks amortize metadata and expose redundancy while increasing buffer, first-record latency, retry/corruption scope, and irrelevant decode for selection.
Verified semantic round trip, frame recovery, and compatibility arguments require declared schema/codec/dictionary/framing metadata and supported reader matrices.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Pipelining, queueing, concurrency, projection, caching, implementation, and contention can invalidate a ranking derived from the sequential approximation.

evidence: Reviewed empty/tiny/huge batches; null-heavy, nested, sorted, random, high/low-cardinality, Unicode, boundary integer, NaN, signed-zero, and wide-record data.
Reviewed incompressible, already-compressed, and encrypted fields; missing/wrong dictionaries; unsupported codecs; truncated/corrupt frames; and lost indexes/footers.
Reviewed malicious lengths, ratios, nesting, varints, duplicate/unknown/removed fields, cross-version/language reserialization, cold start, concurrency, and recovery.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Decoder bounds and corruption behavior are treated as correctness and security obligations rather than benchmark details.

evidence: Traced value/null/order/precision/logical-type semantics through writer schema, encoding, codec, frame, integrity verification, reader schema, and reconstruction.
Checked schema and field-identifier evolution, defaults, unknown-field retention, canonicalization, state-key stability, and rollback readability.
Checked bounded block allocation/decompression/retry, independent decode state, dictionary identity, checksum coverage, attempt publication, and reader support.
invariant_checking.notes: Parse success, wire compatibility, deterministic output, semantic equality, and canonical byte equality are kept as separate claims.

evidence: Reviewed semantic round-trip proof obligations for every admitted value and supported writer/reader schema/language pair.
Reviewed break-even reasoning with explicit sequential assumptions and empirical exceptions for overlap, contention, selection, cache, and queues.
Reviewed frame-recovery and retention-lifetime compatibility arguments, including bounded metadata, valid decode boundaries, checksums, rollback, and old-data expiration.
proof_review.notes: No universal best format, codec, compression level, representation, dictionary, page size, row-group size, or frame size is claimed.

evidence: Audited representation, serialization, deserialization, encoding, compression codec, frame/page/block/batch, schema resolution, canonicalization, dictionary, and amplification terminology.
Confirmed row/column layout, value encoding, general compression, framing, checksumming, and encryption are separate pipeline layers.
Confirmed compression ratio, byte reduction, producer CPU, consumer CPU, throughput, latency, memory, projection, retry scope, and lifecycle cost are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Parquet, Avro, Protocol Buffers, Arrow, Flink, Spark, and Zstandard details are presented as concrete contracts, not interchangeable guarantees.

evidence: Reviewed records and logical/encoded/compressed/physical bytes; block/page/batch sizes; stage-specific CPU/elapsed time; queueing; memory; copies; and I/O.
Reviewed projection/random reads, cache behavior, corruption/checksum/unsupported-codec failures, retries, recovery, producer/consumer fleet, retention, worker-hours, and cost.

Confirmed segmentation by boundary/data/field/type, writer/reader language/version, format/schema/codec/level/dictionary/block, hardware/concurrency, entropy/distribution, percentile, and cache cohort.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Smallest output, producer throughput, one sample ratio, or successful decode is not mislabeled as proof of end-to-end suitability.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed pipeline decomposition, contract lifetime, row/column access, value encodings, codec and block trade-offs, splitability, schema evolution, canonicalization, memory/copies, hostile input, redundant compression, lifecycle weighting, benchmarking, rollout, and observability.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable format/codec metadata, bounded framing, reader inventories, compatibility matrices, representative corpora, producer/consumer measures, projection tests, dual-read canaries, rollback, and retention-aware decoder retirement. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from byte-pipeline vocabulary through performance/correctness models to lifecycle rollout. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover timing, encoding, splitability, canonicalization, unknown fields, hostile expansion, checkpoints, benchmarking, evolution, block design, and migration.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark/Parquet/Avro/Protocol-Buffers/Arrow/Flink/codec maintainer, format/runtime/storage/network/security/performance/economics specialist, production producer or consumer, downstream user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
